27319.etyen:
From Israel (“Israel”) + -itt (“person associated with or originating from”). The base name Israel is the biblical name given to Jacob, transmitted through Latin Israel (“Israel”), from Ancient Greek Ἰσραήλ (Israḗl, “Israel”), from Biblical Hebrew יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yiśrāʾēl, “Israel”); the name was subsequently applied to his descendants. The suffix -itt (“person associated with or originating from”) is from French -ite, from Latin -ita, from Ancient Greek -ίτης (-ítēs, “one belonging to”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk israelitt, Danish israelit, Swedish israelit, German Israelit and English Israelite.

1000119.etyen:
Internationalism, based ultimately on Portuguese Benim, the Portuguese name of the historical kingdom of Benin, from Itsekiri Ubinu. The modern country, formerly called Dahomey, adopted the name in 1975 from the Bight of Benin (Norwegian Beninbukta), which had itself been named after the historical kingdom in present-day Nigeria. The further origin of Ubinu is uncertain; a traditional explanation connects it with ilẹ̀ ìbínú (“land of anger”).
Parallel international adaptations include Norwegian Nynorsk Benin, Danish Benin, Swedish Benin, German Benin, Dutch Benin and English Benin.

1004983.etyen:
Compound of presis (“precise, exact”) + veksel (“bill of exchange”), literally “precise bill of exchange”.
The first element, presis (“precise, exact”), is borrowed from French précis (“precise, exact”), from Latin praecisus (“cut off, shortened”), the perfect passive participle of praecido (“to cut off, shorten”), from prae (“before”) + caedo (“to cut, strike”). The latter continues Proto-Italic *kaidō (“to cut”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kh₂eyd- (“to cut, hew”).
